novelty_flags.label: Bibliography / related_work / Theorem 1 comparison to Gaiffas (2007)
novelty_flags.one_line: Gaiffas2007PointwiseAdaptive conflates the 2005 preprint title “with a degenerate random design” with the distinct 2007 ESAIM article, whose title is “based on inhomogeneous data” and whose pages are 344–364, not 93–115.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Proposition 2 (same-estimator endpoint adaptation)
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The isolated and pervasive minimax benchmarks are imported background from stat_bdd_thickness_estimability_frontier rather than re-established here.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The proposition is limited to simultaneous upper-rate attainment by the displayed estimator; it does not claim a new minimax lower bound or a newly proved endpoint frontier.

source_verification_receipts.version: ESAIM: Probability and Statistics 11 (2007), published version
source_verification_receipts.locator: Bibliographic record, lines 47–54 and 61–102: title, volume 11, pages 344–364, and pointwise adaptive random-design claim.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The 2007 paper is titled “On pointwise adaptive curve estimation based on inhomogeneous data,” studies estimation at a fixed point with unknown design density and local smoothness, and occupies pages 344–364.

source_verification_receipts.version: Statistica Sinica 19 (2009), official supplementary PDF accompanying the published article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes a continuous univariate design density that is positive except at finitely many polynomial zeros and gives a design- and smoothness-adaptive estimator under a spatially dependent uniform metric.

source_verification_receipts.version: ESAIM: Probability and Statistics 18 (2014), published version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies known one-dimensional design densities with a finite number of well-separated polynomial or exponential zeros, global L2 risk, and adaptive wavelet estimators.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference 123(2) (2004), publisher record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article studies Hölder regression in uniform norm and states that its exact minimax constant depends on the minimum design-density value.
The location-based boundary-discontinuity work includes pointwise and uniform convergence-rate results for treatment effects along the assignment boundary.
The published distance-based result assumes a continuous score density bounded above and away from zero and gives its isotropic minimax result on that positive-density class.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:math/0410354, corresponding preprint to the cited 2005 article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives pointwise rates at a regularly varying degenerate-design location, with rate n^{-s/(1+2s+β)} times a slowly varying factor.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Correct Gaiffas2007PointwiseAdaptive everywhere to the published 2007 title and pages 344–364; retain the 2005 degenerate-design paper as its separate comparator.

Add a stated corollary locating the new profile-oracle class relative to the positive-density CTY class and explicitly identify the first nontrivial rate/oracle bound supplied in the polynomial-depletion regime.
Remove the known L and σ implementation limitation by giving a scale-adaptive version, or delimit a concrete application in which defensible envelopes are available.

recommended_next_step: Revise the conflated Gaiffas (2007) citation and sharpen the explicit comparator/regime statement, then advance the field-tier estimator kernel to Stage 0.
